title: Suspected heat illness: first response
banner: This can be a medical emergency. Get medical help now and call the local emergency number.
text: While you wait for help: move the person into shade or indoors. Lay them down and raise their legs. Loosen or remove heavy clothing and any protective gear. Cool them as fast as you can, cool water over the skin, wet cloths on the neck, armpits and groin, fanning for airflow, or a cool shower if one is close. If they are fully awake and not vomiting, give small sips of cool water. Do not give water to someone who is drowsy, confused, or vomiting. Do not leave them alone. Stay with them and keep cooling until medical help arrives.
source: US CDC NIOSH Heat Stress; OSHA-NIOSH Heat Safety Tool; WHO 2018 first-aid guidance
